title: Working habits
summary: Keep the raw data untouched, work on a copy that rebuilds itself, write your steps down, and prove nothing was lost with check totals.
objectives: Lay out an analysis workbook as Raw, Work, Checks and Notes sheets.
Build a working copy with a formula, so the raw data is never edited.
Write check totals that prove no rows or rupees went missing.
Keep a step log someone else could follow.

p: Keep the export exactly as it arrived, on its own sheet. Do all your work on a **copy**, so you can always go back and start again.
Name the sheets so their job is obvious: Raw, Work, Checks, Notes.
If something goes wrong, rebuild Work from Raw: no harm done.
Add the export’s date and source to Notes the moment it arrives.
In real life: deleted the cancelled orders straight from the export to “tidy it”. A month later finance asked how much was cancelled. The rows were gone.

slides.h: A working copy that rebuilds itself
p: Build the Work sheet with a **formula** that reads Raw. Paste next month’s export into Raw and the copy rebuilds itself.
One formula, in Work!A2, and the raw data never changes.
For heavier cleaning, copy Raw and fix the copy, and write each step in Notes.
P5 · Power Query automates this whole routine: one click to refresh.
In real life: replaced an afternoon of copying and deleting with one FILTER per report. Now each week’s export is pasted into Raw and every report updates.

p: A **step log** on a Notes sheet says what you did, why, and how many rows were left. Anyone can follow it, including you in three months’ time.
Write the **why**, not only the what: “left out cancelled because…”.
Rows after each step shows where data was removed.
Assumptions go here too: “Amount includes GST (confirmed by finance)”.
In real life: audits a client’s sales analysis every year. The file with a step log takes an hour to check; the one without takes three days.

check.q: You need a version of the export without cancelled orders. What do you do?
options: Delete the cancelled rows from the export
Filter Raw into a Work sheet with a formula, and note the step
Ask IT for a new export
check.explain: The raw data stays complete; the Work sheet holds what you need, and Notes says how.

why.0: Then the cancelled orders are lost for good.
why.2: Hidden rows still count in many formulas, and are easy to forget.
why.3: You don’t need to: a formula does it.

slides.h: Control totals: nothing lost, nothing added
p: A **control total** compares a count or a sum before and after a step. If the numbers don’t tie, something was lost or doubled.
Rows: before = after + removed.
Money: the same, with SUM instead of counting.
Put checks on their own sheet, so a reviewer looks there first.
In real life: checks that total salary after each step equals the payroll register to the rupee. One day the check said CHECK: an employee had been copied twice.

terms: a count or sum compared before and after a step

p: A check should give a word you can’t miss: **OK** or **CHECK**. For money, allow for tiny rounding differences.
`ABS(…)<0.01` treats 0.000001 left by decimals as zero.
Colour the CHECK cells red with conditional formatting.
One cell can watch them all: `=IF(COUNTIF(B2:B10,"CHECK")=0,"All OK","Fix checks")`.
In real life: won’t open a client’s analysis until the top of the Checks sheet says All OK. If it doesn’t, the file goes straight back.

terms: the size of a number without its sign

slides.h: Check against a number from outside
p: Inside checks prove your steps didn’t lose anything. An **outside check** proves the data itself is complete: compare a total with one you didn’t calculate.
If your total is 3% short of finance’s, find out why before you analyse.
Write each outside check, and its result, in Notes.
A wrong but checked number is rare; an unchecked one is common.
In real life: compared the export total with the payment gateway’s report. The export was ₹2 lakh short: refunds issued by email had never been entered.

check.q: Rows in Raw = 240, rows in Work = 233, rows removed on purpose = 5. What does the rows check show, and what do you do?
options: CHECK: 2 rows are missing; find them before going on
check.explain: 240 ≠ 233 + 5. Two rows vanished without a reason: find out where.

why.0: “Close enough” is how errors get into reports.
why.2: Smaller is fine only if every removed row is accounted for.
why.3: Never change data to make a check pass.

tasks.prompt: On **Work**, in **A2**, copy every order line from Raw **except cancelled ones**, with one formula.
hints: FILTER(what to return, which rows to keep).

tasks.prompt: On **Checks**, in **B2**, count the rows in **Raw**.

hints: Work!A2# means the whole spilled column; or count filled cells in Work!A2:A241.

tasks.prompt: In **Checks!B4**, count the **Cancelled** rows in Raw.
hints: Status is column L of Raw.

tasks.prompt: In **Checks!B5**, show **OK** if rows in Raw = rows in Work + cancelled rows, and **CHECK** if not.

expect.regexMsg: Compare the rows in Raw (B2) with Work plus cancelled (B3+B4).

tasks.prompt: In **Checks!B8**, add up the **Amount** column of Work.
In **Checks!B10**, show **OK** if the amount in Raw (B7) minus Work (B8) minus cancelled (B9) is less than 0.01 away from zero, otherwise **CHECK**.
hints: ABS gives the size of the difference.

real.title: Profile the whole year
steps: Download **Taraloom orders FY2025-26**: 10,000 order lines on the **Orders** sheet. Don’t change anything on Orders.

On **Profile**, put a formula in each cell of **B2:B10** for the label beside it: rows, distinct orders, distinct customers, first and last date, rows with no city, exact duplicate rows, total amount, and the delivered share of the amount.
Use whole columns of data, like Orders!A2:A10001. Format dates as dates and the share as a percentage.
On **Questions**, write five sharp questions this data could answer in **A2:A6**: each with a measure, a group, a period and, if needed, a filter.
On **Notes**, write at least one step: what you did, why, and the rows after it.
Save as .xlsx and upload it here.

quiz.q: Which sheet should never be edited?
Rows in Raw 240, Work 235, removed on purpose 5. The rows check shows…
Why use ABS(B7-B8-B9)<0.01 instead of B7=B8+B9 for money?
options: Decimals can leave tiny differences like 0.0000001
quiz.explain: A rounding crumb shouldn’t turn a check red.

options: The whole answer spilled from A2
quiz.explain: The # follows the spill, however many rows it has.

quiz.q: Your export total is ₹2 lakh below the payment gateway’s report. What next?
options: Add ₹2 lakh to make it match
Find the reason before analysing, and note it
quiz.explain: An outside check that fails means the data may be incomplete.

quiz.q: Which is the best reason to build Work with a formula rather than by copying and deleting?
options: It rebuilds itself when a new export is pasted into Raw
quiz.explain: Repeatable work: paste the new export, and everything follows.

points: Four sheets: **Raw** (untouched), **Work**, **Checks**, **Notes**.
Build Work with a formula such as **FILTER(Raw…)**, so it rebuilds itself.
**Control totals** (rows and money) say OK or CHECK; write every step in Notes.
